title: Bisect retained TensorView entries by unique semantic claim key
masterplan_authority: Revision 11 / Version 2.2.0 / Gate 1 — Renovation and owner-directed Genesis
finding: TensorView.index_coordinate() located a retained entry by bisecting with the complete _entry_order tuple. TensorView construction already forbids duplicate coordinate/relation claims, so coordinates plus relation are a unique semantic claim key. Reading masked, value and evidence_sha256s during every binary-search comparison was therefore redundant payload work before the existing exact retained-entry equality check.
primary_claim: TensorView.index_coordinate() now bisects the canonical retained entry tuple using SparseTensorEntry.semantic_key, which is the already-existing coordinates/relation claim key. It still performs exact entry equality after locating the claim, so an entry with the same semantic claim but changed scalar, mask or evidence payload remains rejected as not retained.
gardener_decision: Reuse the existing SparseTensorEntry.semantic_key and the uniqueness invariant already enforced during TensorView construction rather than adding a secondary lookup index, cache, registry or alternate tensor representation. Preserve the exact retained-entry equality check as the payload/evidence boundary after binary search.
acceptance: retained entry lookup is located by the already-unique coordinate/relation semantic claim
binary search does not require non-semantic scalar, mask or evidence payload reads for every comparison
exact entry equality remains required after semantic-key lookup
same-claim entries with altered payload remain fail-closed as not retained
